extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and packaging press releases and related PR materials, including newsworthiness criteria, medium-specific packaging, process framework (RACE), and quality standards from Cutlip & Center's textbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know what information will attract media attention
rubrics_metrics.description: PR practitioners must know what information will attract media attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify facts, events, or angles that meet reporters' needs; this is the foundational skill for selecting news to pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify a newsworthy angle and lead
rubrics_metrics.description: PR practitioners must identify a newsworthy angle and lead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a clear, compelling lead that emphasizes the most newsworthy element (per news values) to engage journalists and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write and package appropriately for each medium
rubrics_metrics.description: PR practitioners must write and package the information appropriately for each medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt tone, format, length, and supporting materials (photos, sound bites, scripts) to the expectations of print, broadcast, blogs, and online outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print media packaging
rubrics_metrics.description: For print media, provide a news release with feature story, photographs, and a media kit with detailed background information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include high-resolution photos, press kits with backgrounders and fact sheets, and formatted copy suited to newspaper/magazine editing workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast media and blogs packaging
rubrics_metrics.description: For broadcast media and blogs, supply broadcast-style news scripts, recorded interviews or 'sound bites', video news releases (VNR), and a media kit with material suitable for broadcast or Internet posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide short, quotable sound bites and ready-to-use audiovisual assets; format copy for read-aloud clarity and time constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact (news value)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how many people are affected or the magnitude of the effect; emphasize consequences and measurable effects in the lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness (news value)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie releases to current events, deadlines, or an appropriate news cycle; emphasize ‘why now’ to increase pickup likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence (news value)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight involvement of well-known figures or institutions to increase news interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity (news value)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize local angles or effects for local media; tailor releases to geographic relevance of target outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bizarreness (news value)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note novel, quirky, or unexpected elements that make a story stand out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict (news value)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories involving disagreement, controversy, or competition often attract coverage; present conflict responsibly and accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency (news value)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect the piece to broader ongoing issues or trends to show relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human interest (news value)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use human-focused narratives, anecdotes, or emotional elements to engage audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research (RACE framework)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct audience analysis and situation research to identify objectives and appropriate messaging before drafting releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action planning (RACE framework)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop strategic objectives, target media lists, timing, and tactical plans (including releases and supporting materials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication (RACE framework)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Execute the plan via press releases, interviews, media kits, and other outreach adapted to each medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation (RACE framework)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess media pickup, audience reach, message penetration, and outcomes relative to objectives to inform future practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthy (press release quality standard)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A press release should meet one or more of the identified news values (impact, timeliness, prominence, proximity, bizarreness, conflict, currency, human interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate (press release quality standard)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all facts, figures, names, and claims are checkable; avoid speculation and correct errors promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely (press release quality standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely — releases at right news cycle moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule distribution to coincide with relevant news windows and reporters' deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted (press release quality standard)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor content and distribution lists to the specific outlets and reporters most likely to care about the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical (press release quality standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical — transparent about source and intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose sponsorship, avoid deceptive practices, and follow professional ethical norms rather than hiding intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional (press release quality standard)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accepted journalistic style and formatting, clean writing, and correct grammar to facilitate editorial use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-way symmetric communication model (Excellence theory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-way symmetric communication model — PR should be two-way (listening and responding), symmetric (mutual understanding, not propaganda), strategic (tied to org goals), and diverse (representing all stakeholders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design releases and broader PR activity to promote mutual understanding and dialogue rather than one-way persuasion; align messages with organizational strategy and consider diverse stakeholder perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press releases should serve mutual understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should serve mutual understanding rather than one-way persuasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame communications to facilitate dialogue and relationship-building with publics, not merely to push an organization’s agenda.
